ideal: Features are visual cards; bugs stay in issues. A card in progress has an open pull request, and Done cards link a merged one.

parts.ideal: A feature is a draft card: a picture of its metric and steps, a table, at most 75 words
parts.setup: Add it on the board; convert it to an issue, with its area label, when its pull request opens

parts.ideal: One image per card: its pillar, a meter from now to goal, its steps left to right
parts.setup: Run the card picture tool, push the file to the cards branch, link it by its raw address

parts.ideal: Status, Pillar and Area; each fact lives in one field
parts.setup: Create them with the Projects API; show Linked pull requests on every card

parts.ideal: Board, Backlog, Shipped and Stuck: each is the search behind one metric
parts.setup: Create views with the REST views endpoint; set no column limit

parts.ideal: Added sets Todo, a linked pull request In Progress, closed or merged Done, reopened Todo
parts.setup: Turn each on in the Workflows page; GitHub offers no API to edit them

parts.ideal: Charts of cards by status and pillar, by area and status, and the burn up
parts.setup: Create them in the Insights page; never archive a card, since archived cards leave the charts

parts.ideal: One fresh session per card, ended at the merge; the card names its goal, its files and a check
parts.setup: Start a session per card in its own worktree; merge a green pull request before opening another

parts.ideal: No count limit on cards; a card in progress has an open pull request, and open pull requests carry the limit
parts.setup: Move a waiting card back to Todo and name what it waits on

quality: Every open card shows a picture in few words, no bug sits on the board, and each card in progress has an open pull request.
speed: A card is done within three days of its first pull request, and none stays in progress past a week.
consumption: A card's pull requests use no more runner time than a typical merged pull request.
